anatomy.title: Prosecution Beyond Law: An Anatomy of Abuse
anatomy.subtitle: One transaction: a lawful commercial act according to final court rulings, and 'fraud' according to the prosecution.
anatomy.text: This archive is not merely a defense position; it is a documentary record of a systemic collapse of the rule of law. In the case of Dmitry Lagovsky, extradition is being weaponized to legitimize arbitrary prosecution. This platform brings together primary evidence — from final arbitration judgments that upheld the transaction at the highest level to a chronicle of the 'flagrant denial of justice' within Russia. When domestic safeguards are systematically bypassed, international oversight remains the final barrier against wrongful conviction.
anatomy.manifesto: To treat this extradition request as lawful is to establish a dangerous precedent: it transforms international cooperation into a mechanism for cross-border repression, where political expediency and falsified records outweigh human life and the principle of legality.

legal.title: Legal Dissonance
legal.text: Arbitration courts at all levels, including the Russian Supreme Court, confirmed the transaction was lawful and economically sound. Yet, investigators have characterized the same acts as 'embezzlement,' ignoring the principles of res judicata and judicial finality. The prosecution's core 'evidence' — a requirement for fair market value — is absurdly framed as intent to commit a crime.
legal.question: Can compliance with the law and a demand for fair market value be used as evidence of a criminal conspiracy?

international.title: International Standards
international.text: Serbia, Interpol (CCF), UNHCR, and the ECHR. International institutions act as a filter against abuse. When a requesting state flouts its own laws, the burden of protecting fundamental rights shifts to the international community and the principle of non-refoulement.

actors.title: Registry of Responsibility
actors.text: This case was constructed by identifiable individuals, from those who initiated the corporate conflict to the officials signing boilerplate refusals. Documenting their roles is essential for future accountability and the restoration of justice.

flagrant.title: Flagrant Denial of Justice
flagrant.text: The systemic refusal to review defense complaints on their merits constitutes a separate violation of Article 6 ECHR. Not a single supervisory body in Russia has examined the defense's arguments, substituting justice with bureaucratic redirection. This renders a fair trial impossible in the event of surrender.

news.title: Legal Vacuum: Six Months Without a Ministerial Decision
news.desc: The judicial phase has ended with a formal approval, but the final act of extradition remains unsigned. Lagovsky remains in a legal limbo, and his family in a state of indefinite uncertainty.

news.title: UNHCR Memorandum: Non-refoulement and Humanitarian Risks
news.desc: International monitors record a systemic failure of protection. The risk of violating Articles 3 and 8 ECHR necessitates a halt to extradition pending the Administrative Court's final ruling.

news.title: Asylum Appeal Dismissed
news.desc: The extra-judicial commission upheld the initial refusal. The case now moves to the Administrative Court, the final domestic instance for asylum review.

news.title: Refugee Status Refused: Ignoring Foreseeable Risks
news.desc: The authority acknowledged the risk of forced mobilisation but refused to classify it as persecution, diverging from international protection standards.

news.title: Supreme Court: Formalism Over Justice
news.desc: Request for Protection of Legality dismissed. The Court avoided assessing the merits of the case, limiting its review to the formal documentation package provided by the requesting party.

news.title: Process Without Defense: Court Ignores Arbitration Rulings
news.desc: N1 report: Serbian justice refuses to consider exculpatory documents from Russia, focusing solely on the prosecutorial narrative from Moscow.

news.title: Family at Risk: Between the Frontline and Deportation
news.desc: Nova.rs on the humanitarian dimension. How extradition destroys children's lives and violates the right to family life under Article 8 ECHR.

news.title: Appellate Court Approves Extradition
news.desc: Second-instance court confirmed the extradition grounds. The case has moved to the political level, awaiting the Justice Minister's signature.

news.title: CCF: Defense Challenges Red Notice
news.desc: Evidence provided showing lack of executive authority and the civil-law nature of the contract. Challenging the notice as politically motivated.

news.title: Interpol Begins Review of Lagovsky Case
news.desc: The Commission for the Control of Interpol's Files (CCF) registered the complaint. This is the first step toward deleting data based on human rights violations.

news.title: Res Judicata: Transaction Ruled Lawful
news.desc: Fundamental Arbitration Court ruling: the land sale was legitimate, and no harm was caused to shareholders. A direct refutation of the indictment's core premise.
